question: If /design stops being a door, where does /sorted's `routed_out / back-to-design` disposition route TO? The exit names a destination; if that destination is not a berth, the exit either needs a new referent or the vocabulary needs to change.
whats_beyond: MEASURED 2026-08-11: /sorted has fired back-to-design exactly ONCE in 27 firings, and ZERO design berths carry `entering_from: sorted:<berth>`. So the back edge exists on both sides of the seam and has never once been walked — the one node sent back never arrived. That is true TODAY, with the door in place, which means the question is not created by killing the door: killing it only makes an already-dead edge honest. Beyond here: whether 'back to design' is a route at all, or whether a failed completeness check simply leaves the node uncast and in hand — in which case the disposition is naming a journey that was always just 'not yet'.
source: The /design conversation, 2026-08-11 — raised by CC as the third cost of killing the skill and left as prose in a turn. Filed under decisions/2026-08-11-open-questions-land-with-cc-and-surface-at-the-hook.json.

resolved.answer: back-to-design was naming a destination that was ruled away (2026-08-11: 'that was the last argument for keeping /design as a door, and this ruling removes it') and was never walked (1 disposition in 79 firings, 0 arrivals at /design). The disposition is renamed to 'not-ready': a completeness red leaves the node uncast and in hand — there is no separate design step to route back to. The node stays with the operator, who re-questions the gap or escalates.
resolved.what_changed: sorted/door.py: 'back-to-design' → 'not-ready' in the gate logic. SKILL.md: three references updated. intention+why.json: disposition field. proofs/test_sorted_door.py: test vocabulary. proofs/PROOF.md. design/probes/design_return_trip.py: reads both old and new vocabulary so existing berths still count. All proofs GREEN (32 teeth).
resolved.what_remains: The one historical berth carrying disposition 'back-to-design' in instance-space is not rewritten — it is a record of truth (Law 7). The design_return_trip probe now reads both 'back-to-design' and 'not-ready' so its promised_returns count stays honest across the rename. The probe's existence question ('is the return trip countable?') is answered by the ruling that killed the door: the return trip cannot happen because there is no door to return to, so the probe's clear condition (returns >= 1) will never fire. Whether the probe should be retired is the probe's own ticket's question, not this one's.
